paper.title: Subjective well-being and chronic illnesses: A combined survey and register study
paper.code_data_availability: Data availability statement (p. 16): 'Due to Danish Data Protection Legislation, only Danish research environments can be granted authorisation to Danish administrative registers.' No DST project number and no replication code are reported. …

registers.role: treatment: hospital contacts used by the Danish Health Data Authority algorithm to identify the six chronic illnesses; also the source for date of diagnosis
variables_mentioned: ICD-10 diagnosis codes (example given for osteoporosis: M80, M81, M82)

registers.role: treatment: redeemed prescriptions used by the Danish Health Data Authority algorithm to identify the six chronic illnesses; also the source for date of diagnosis
variables_mentioned: ATC codes (example given for osteoporosis: M05BA01, M05BA04, M05BA06, M05BA07, M05BB01, M05BB03, M05BX03, G03XC01, H05AA02, H05AA03)

registers.name_in_paper: the Danish registers / national register data (socio-demographic information; register not named individually)
registers.role: controls and sample frame: gender, age, ethnicity, living situation, number of children, municipality of residence, education, labour market attachment, wealth

registers.name_in_paper: Charlson Comorbidity Index (register-based, used in a robustness check)
registers.role: robustness: restricting the control group to individuals with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of zero

linkages: Survey responses linked to national register data via the unique individual personal identification number assigned to all individuals with permanent residence in Denmark

Chronic illness identified by combining the Danish National Patient Register and the Danish National Prescription Registry with the Danish Health Data Authority (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen, 2019) algorithm

sample.universe: A representative group of Danish citizens aged 50-80 years, invited to a web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019
selection_rules: 6,807 individuals (45%) returned a fully completed questionnaire
80 individuals who had lived abroad for extended periods of time during 2014-2018 are excluded
24 excluded due to non-response on the well-being questions ('do not know' and 'refuse to answer')
460 excluded due to non-response on key variables
The control group consists of individuals with none of the selected chronic illnesses
Resulting analysis sample: 1,495 individuals with a chronic illness and 4,748 controls
Robustness check: 541 individuals dropped when the control group is restricted to a Charlson Comorbidity Index of zero
Regressions involving labour market attachment are run on the subgroup aged below 65 years
sample.period: Survey collected spring 2019; chronic illness status evaluated 1 March 2019; demographics 1 January 2019; education 1 October 2018; wealth and labour market attachment 31 December 2018

construction_notes: All SWB scores are converted into a 0-100 point scale
General SWB: 'How satisfied are you with your life as a whole?' on an 11-point end-defined scale from 0 to 10

Seven domain-specific SWB items from the Personal Wellbeing Index: standard of living, health, achieving in life, relationships, safety, community connectedness, future security; the authors refrain from summing them into one PWI score because no preference weights are established
HRQoL assessed with EQ-5D-5L using Danish weights (Jensen et al., 2021)
Chronic illness = asthma, COPD, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, type 1 diabetes or type 2 diabetes, identified with the Danish Health Data Authority algorithm; cancer deliberately excluded
Chronic illness status evaluated on 1 March 2019; duration = years since first relevant hospital contact or first relevant prescription redemption
Age is rescaled by dividing with 5
Wealth is net worth in DKK 100,000: assets excluding private pensions minus debts
Labour market attachment = 1 if not working and under 65 years; 0 if working and under 65, or 65 years or older
Smoking: 'yes' and 'no, I quit' combined into an ever-smoker dummy
Weekly exercise is reverse scored so that a higher score indicates less exercise per week
Health literacy score: first four HLS-EU-Q16 items, 'very easy'/'easy' coded 1, summed to 0-4
Internal health locus of control: six items of the Wallston et al. (1978) scale on a 6-point Likert scale summed to 6-36
Big Five traits measured with the TIPI: reverse-scored items recoded, then the two items per scale averaged
A significance level of 5% is applied, with results also verified after Bonferroni correction

claims.statement: Among Danish 50-80 year olds, having at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses is associated with a lower score on general subjective well-being (general life satisfaction), conditional on a full set of socio-demographic, lifestyle, skill, preference and personality covariates.

treatment.label: Having at least one chronic illness

register_source.value: Danish National Patient Register (hospital contacts) and Danish National Prescription Registry (redeemed prescriptions), combined with the chronic-illness algorithm of The Danish Health Data Authority (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen, 2019).

definition.value: Combined dummy variable equal to one if the individual has at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses (asthma, COPD, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes); the control group is individuals with none of the selected chronic illnesses.

timing.value: Chronic illness status is evaluated on 1 March 2019; date of diagnosis is the first relevant hospital contact or first redemption of a relevant prescription.

register_source.value: Not a register variable: self-reported item in the web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019 through the digital mailbox for official governmental communication.

definition.value: Measured with the life satisfaction question 'How satisfied are you with your life as a whole?' on an 11-point end-defined response scale from 0 (extremely dissatisfied) to 10 (extremely satisfied), converted into a 0-100 point scale.

timing.value: Measured in the spring 2019 cross-sectional survey, i.e. contemporaneously with chronic-illness status (evaluated 1 March 2019); no pre/post timing.

units.value: points on the 0-100 SWB scale

magnitude.interpretation: a reduction of 2.5% in average general SWB for those with chronic illness compared to the control group

estimand.target_population: Danish citizens aged 50-80 years, comparing those with at least one of the six selected chronic illnesses with those with none of them

population.description: Danish citizens aged 50-80 who responded to the spring 2019 Statistics Denmark web survey and could be linked to the national registers: 1,495 individuals with at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses and 4,748 controls with none of them.
population.period: Survey collected spring 2019; register variables measured 1 October 2018 - 1 March 2019
subgroups_defined: individuals with at least one chronic illness
control group: individuals with none of the selected chronic illnesses
population.selection: Respondents to a web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019: 15,072 invited, 6,807 (45%) returned a fully completed questionnaire; 80 who had lived abroad 2014-2018, 24 with non-response on the well-being questions and 460 with non-response on key variables were excluded.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional between-person variation in register-identified chronic illness status (evaluated 1 March 2019) among survey respondents aged 50-80; no exogenous variation is exploited and the authors explicitly refrain from a causal interpretation.

key_assumptions.assumption: The association between chronic illness and well-being may be confounded; the authors seek to overcome this by including a comprehensive set of covariates, and concede that unobserved common causes remain.
key_assumptions.supported_by: stepwise inclusion of covariates (Fig. A1, Supplementary Appendix), where the estimate moves between 4.3 and 2.6 points and the estimates are reported as not statistically significantly different from each other

implies_edges.to: having at least one chronic illness

key_assumptions.assumption: The direction of causation is not identified: potential reverse causality from well-being to health means the estimate is interpreted as an association only.
key_assumptions.supported_by: the authors' argument that a negative association is also observed for type 1 diabetes, an illness they describe as random because of its strong genetic component

key_assumptions.assumption: Covariates are measured after diagnosis, so personal characteristics (living situation, labour market attachment, wealth, lifestyle, locus of control, health literacy, risk aversion) may themselves be consequences of health state.
key_assumptions.supported_by: no test offered; the authors note the Big Five traits are most likely stable over time (Cobb-Clark & Schurer, 2012)

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on responding to the 2019 survey (45% of those invited) and on item non-response exclusions; non-responders are assumed not to drive the results.
key_assumptions.supported_by: regressions weighted by Statistics Denmark survey weights show a similar pattern (results available upon request)

key_assumptions.assumption: The conditional mean of well-being is linear and additive in the chronic-illness indicator and in the covariate vector, with a single coefficient common to all individuals.
key_assumptions.supported_by: robustness check defining continuous and ordinal covariates by their median value instead of entering them as continuous variables

heterogeneity.finding: We find indications of variation in the degree to which chronic illness is associated with lower SWB across types of chronic illnesses, although the differences are not statistically significant in most cases.
Non-ethnic Danish background, openness to experiences and internal health locus of control are associated with a smaller detriment in general SWB; none survives the Bonferroni correction.

evidence.annotation: Note: The figure displays regression coefficients and their 95% confidence intervals (robust standard errors). We regress chronic illness on the seven domains of SWB and general SWB for each chronic illness and a combined variable for having at least one chronic illness. Specifications include the covariates: gender, age, non-ethnic Danish, living alone, number of children, municipality, years of education, labour market attachment, wealth in DKK 100,000, BMI, ever smoker, alcohol consumption, diet, exercise, extraversion, agreeableness, conscientiousness, emotional stability, openness to experiences, planning horizon, internal health locus of control, health literacy, and risk aversion.

evidence.how: The text prints the difference in general SWB as '2.0 points' as a reduction for those with chronic illness; Fig. 1 plots the corresponding coefficient below the zero line, so the regression coefficient is -2.0 points on the 0-100 scale.

claims.statement: Among Danish 50-80 year olds, having at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses is associated with a lower score on swb in the achieving in life domain, conditional on a full set of socio-demographic, lifestyle, skill, preference and personality covariates.

treatment.label: Having at least one chronic illness

register_source.value: Danish National Patient Register (hospital contacts) and Danish National Prescription Registry (redeemed prescriptions), combined with the chronic-illness algorithm of The Danish Health Data Authority (Sundhedsdatastyrelsen, 2019).

definition.value: Combined dummy variable equal to one if the individual has at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses (asthma, COPD, rheumatoid arthritis, osteoporosis, type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes); the control group is individuals with none of the selected chronic illnesses.

timing.value: Chronic illness status is evaluated on 1 March 2019; date of diagnosis is the first relevant hospital contact or first redemption of a relevant prescription.

outcome.label: SWB in the achieving in life domain

register_source.value: Not a register variable: self-reported item in the web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019 through the digital mailbox for official governmental communication.

definition.value: Domain-specific satisfaction item of the Personal Wellbeing Index (PWI), similar phrasing to the general life satisfaction question, converted into a 0-100 point scale.

timing.value: Measured in the spring 2019 cross-sectional survey, i.e. contemporaneously with chronic-illness status (evaluated 1 March 2019); no pre/post timing.

units.value: points on the 0-100 SWB scale

estimand.target_population: Danish citizens aged 50-80 years, comparing those with at least one of the six selected chronic illnesses with those with none of them

population.description: Danish citizens aged 50-80 who responded to the spring 2019 Statistics Denmark web survey and could be linked to the national registers: 1,495 individuals with at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses and 4,748 controls with none of them.
population.period: Survey collected spring 2019; register variables measured 1 October 2018 - 1 March 2019
subgroups_defined: individuals with at least one chronic illness
control group: individuals with none of the selected chronic illnesses
population.selection: Respondents to a web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019: 15,072 invited, 6,807 (45%) returned a fully completed questionnaire; 80 who had lived abroad 2014-2018, 24 with non-response on the well-being questions and 460 with non-response on key variables were excluded.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional between-person variation in register-identified chronic illness status (evaluated 1 March 2019) among survey respondents aged 50-80; no exogenous variation is exploited and the authors explicitly refrain from a causal interpretation.

key_assumptions.assumption: The association between chronic illness and well-being may be confounded; the authors seek to overcome this by including a comprehensive set of covariates, and concede that unobserved common causes remain.
key_assumptions.supported_by: stepwise inclusion of covariates (Fig. A1, Supplementary Appendix), where the estimate moves between 4.3 and 2.6 points and the estimates are reported as not statistically significantly different from each other

implies_edges.to: having at least one chronic illness
SWB in the achieving in life domain

key_assumptions.supported_by: no test offered; the authors note the Big Five traits are most likely stable over time (Cobb-Clark & Schurer, 2012)

key_assumptions.supported_by: regressions weighted by Statistics Denmark survey weights show a similar pattern (results available upon request)

register_source.value: Danish administrative registers (register not named individually in the paper); demographic variables assessed on 1 January 2019. Chronic illness status comes from the Danish National Patient Register and the Danish National Prescription Registry.

definition.value: Product of the dummy for having at least one chronic illness and the personal characteristic: Register-based ethnicity entered as a dummy (ethnic Danish vs non-ethnic Danish); assessed on 1 January 2019. The coefficient beta_{3,p} is the additional impact of the personal characteristic on SWB due to chronic illness.

timing.value: Both components measured cross-sectionally in 2018-2019, after diagnosis.

register_source.value: Not a register variable: self-reported item in the web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019 through the digital mailbox for official governmental communication.

definition.value: Measured with the life satisfaction question 'How satisfied are you with your life as a whole?' on an 11-point end-defined response scale from 0 (extremely dissatisfied) to 10 (extremely satisfied), converted into a 0-100 point scale.

timing.value: Measured in the spring 2019 cross-sectional survey, i.e. contemporaneously with chronic-illness status (evaluated 1 March 2019); no pre/post timing.

units.value: points on the 0-100 general SWB scale per unit of the personal characteristic, additional for the chronically ill

estimand.target_population: Danish citizens aged 50-80 years; the contrast is between chronically ill and control individuals at different levels of the personal characteristic

population.description: Danish citizens aged 50-80 who responded to the spring 2019 Statistics Denmark web survey and could be linked to the national registers: 1,495 individuals with at least one of six register-identified chronic illnesses and 4,748 controls with none of them.
population.period: Survey collected spring 2019; register variables measured 1 October 2018 - 1 March 2019
subgroups_defined: individuals with at least one chronic illness
control group: individuals with none of the selected chronic illnesses
population.selection: Respondents to a web survey administered by Statistics Denmark in spring 2019: 15,072 invited, 6,807 (45%) returned a fully completed questionnaire; 80 who had lived abroad 2014-2018, 24 with non-response on the well-being questions and 460 with non-response on key variables were excluded.

identification.source_of_variation: Cross-sectional between-person variation in personal characteristics interacted with register-identified chronic illness status among survey respondents aged 50-80; no exogenous variation is exploited and the authors explicitly refrain from a causal interpretation.

key_assumptions.assumption: The association between chronic illness and well-being may be confounded; the authors seek to overcome this by including a comprehensive set of covariates, and concede that unobserved common causes remain.
key_assumptions.supported_by: stepwise inclusion of covariates (Fig. A1, Supplementary Appendix), where the estimate moves between 4.3 and 2.6 points and the estimates are reported as not statistically significantly different from each other

implies_edges.to: interaction: having at least one chronic illness x Non-ethnic Danish

key_assumptions.assumption: The direction of causation is not identified: potential reverse causality from well-being to health means the estimate is interpreted as an association only.
key_assumptions.supported_by: the authors' argument that a negative association is also observed for type 1 diabetes, an illness they describe as random because of its strong genetic component

key_assumptions.assumption: Covariates are measured after diagnosis, so personal characteristics (living situation, labour market attachment, wealth, lifestyle, locus of control, health literacy, risk aversion) may themselves be consequences of health state.
key_assumptions.supported_by: no test offered; the authors note the Big Five traits are most likely stable over time (Cobb-Clark & Schurer, 2012)

key_assumptions.assumption: The estimation sample is conditioned on responding to the 2019 survey (45% of those invited) and on item non-response exclusions; non-responders are assumed not to drive the results.
key_assumptions.supported_by: regressions weighted by Statistics Denmark survey weights show a similar pattern (results available upon request)

key_assumptions.assumption: The conditional mean of well-being is linear and additive in the chronic-illness indicator and in the covariate vector, with a single coefficient common to all individuals.
key_assumptions.supported_by: robustness check defining continuous and ordinal covariates by their median value instead of entering them as continuous variables

potential reverse causality between SWB and health
endogeneity of personal characteristics, which are measured after diagnosis
overcontrolling
sample selection / non-response to the survey
multicollinearity between covariates
multiplicity (inflation of the type I error rate)
relatively small sample
robustness_checks: Bonferroni correction for multiplicity
stepwise inclusion of covariates (Fig. A1, Supplementary Appendix)
continuous and ordinal covariates defined by their median value instead of entered as continuous
adding a dummy variable for having multiple chronic illnesses
restricting the control group to individuals with a Charlson Comorbidity Index of zero (drops 541 individuals)
weighting regressions by survey weights provided by Statistics Denmark
adding survey completion time as a covariate
AIC and BIC comparison across the stepwise models (results available upon request)
multicollinearity testing (results available upon request)
unresolved_confounders: reverse causality: the authors state they cannot identify a causal direction

personal characteristics are measured after diagnosis and may themselves be influenced by health state (living situation, labour market attachment, wealth, lifestyle, locus of control, health literacy, risk aversion)
sample selection if non-responders differ systematically from responders
unobservable characteristics not associated with health (e.g. religious beliefs, larger family networks) invoked to explain higher SWB among non-ethnic Danes

estimation.specification: Eq. (2): OLS of general SWB on the personal characteristic, the chronic-illness dummy, their interaction and the remaining covariates W_i; beta_{3,p} is the parameter of interest; robust standard errors
estimation.weights: None in the main specification (survey weights are used only in a robustness check)

sample_n.value: 6,243 individuals (1,495 with a chronic illness and 4,748 controls)

source_table.value: Fig. 2 (p. 10), 'Non-ethnic Danish' series

heterogeneity.finding: Statistically significant at the 5% level but not after Bonferroni correction.
